title: Edge-prefetch surgical toollet contracts (rough brainstorm)
summary: Working notes exploring a lightweight contract between hosted streaming responses and "surgical" toollets (fine-grained tool calls). Goal: minimize wasted tokens and latency by prefetching only likely tool outputs and exposing an ergonomic SDK surface for partial JSON streams.
problem_statement: Large streaming responses with embedded tool calls cause wasted compute and awkward client UX: full tool execution is expensive and often unnecessary, clients can't gracefully present partial structured results, SDK ergonomics for optional prefetching are inconsistent across platforms.
goals: 1) Define a minimal toollet contract that allows the server to indicate candidate tool invocations and confidence. 2) Specify prefetch hints so the runtime can optionally warm tool results without blocking the main stream. 3) Propose SDK surfaces (JS + Python) that let apps opt into partial JSON tiles and resume/commit semantics. 4) Add telemetry hooks to measure cost savings and UX latency impact.
non_goals: 1) Full design of backend autoscaler for tool pools. 2) Enterprise security review for on-prem toollets (separate doc). 3) Rewriting existing typed-stream protocol (we should be backward-compatible).
user_stories: As a product engineer, I want the hosted API to advertise potential tool calls early so my client UI can show placeholders and avoid surprises.
As an SDK user, I want a simple API to accept partial JSON frames and render them progressively, falling back to placeholders until final tool results arrive.
As an ops engineer, I want telemetry that shows how many prefetched toollet executions saved token cost or reduced end-to-end latency.
As a mobile developer, I want prefetch to be opt-in per-channel to avoid unnecessary mobile data consumption.
proposed_api_surface: High-level idea: extend current streaming responses with an optional 'toollet_hint' envelope. Toollet_hint includes: id, tool_type, confidence(0-1), cost_estimate_tokens, prefetchable: true|false, resume_token (opaque). Example surfaces: - streamingChunk.toollet_hint -> client chooses PRELOAD | DEFER | IGNORE. - SDK helper: await stream.prefetchToollet(id, mode) returns immediate placeholder handle with .commit() when ready.
streaming_behavior_notes: Keep main token stream first-class and low-latency. Toollet hints should never block text emission. If prefetch is enabled the runtime may schedule tool execution in background; prefetched results will be delivered as sidecar events with commit IDs. If prefetch fails, emit a compact failure frame rather than stalling the primary stream.
tool_call_contract: Toollets are small, idempotent operations (retrieval, simple API call, db lookup) with bounded latency. Contract fields (all opaque strings/short numbers in first version): toollet_id, signature_version, suggested_cache_ttl_seconds, estimated_token_cost, canonical_output_schema (optional JSONSchema id). Tool runtime must accept a resume_token to reconcile partial results. Security note: toollets that access customer data must be flagged and disallowed from speculative prefetch by default.
sdk_ergonomics_notes: JS SDK: stream.on('toollet', handler) where handler receives hint object and returns {mode: 'defer'|'prefetch'|'prefetch-background'}. Provide convenience helpers: stream.prefetch(id) -> Promise<Placeholder>. Placeholder has .on('update', cb) and .final() promise. Python SDK: async iterator yields frames and ToolHint objects; helper function prefetch_toollet(stream, id, mode) returns async generator of partial results. Keep surface small; avoid forcing app developers to manage tokens directly.
telemetry_and_observability: Emit telemetry events: toollet_hint_emitted, prefetch_requested, prefetch_executed, prefetch_failed, tool_commit_received, tool_ignored. Capture fields: model_id, route, toollet_id (hashed), client_id (anonymized), latency_ms for commit, token_cost_estimated, token_cost_actual, prefetch_mode. Add dials in Console for sampling prefetch events and for per-route prefetch budget.
rollout_and_metrics: Phase 1 (internal beta): enable on 5% of hosted routes; measure 1) average additional tokens consumed per session 2) mean time-to-first-meaningful-update in client UI 3) percent of prefetched toollets that were ultimately necessary. Success targets: reduce median client perceived fill-time by 20% with <5% increase in token cost. Phase 2: opt-in by account; Phase 3: default-on with conservative prefetch budgets.
open_questions: How to represent confidence thresholds consistently across model families? fractional vs. categorical?
Do we allow multi-tool prefetch pipelines (toollet A prefetches B) or ban by policy?
What prefetch budgeting primitives do we expose to customers (tokens per minute per route)?
How to prevent speculative prefetch from creating data exfiltration vectors (audit and opt-out)?
Edge case: if a prefetched tool result diverges from final model output, how do we surface reconciliation to clients?
